MSFT.rationale: Microsoft presents a solid fundamental case with strong revenue growth (+18.3% YoY in Q3 FY2026), excellent profitability (46.3% operating margin, 35.7% net margin), and a fortress balance sheet ($78.3B cash vs $40.3B debt). Azure's 40% growth and the AI business reaching a $37B annual run rate (+123% YoY) demonstrate durable competitive positioning. However, the stock is not a screaming bargain — at 30.4x trailing P/E it sits near the middle of its 25.4–42.8x 12-month range, roughly in line with its 5-year median rather than deeply discounted. The massive $190B 2026 capex plan creates near-term margin pressure (gross margin fell to 67.6% from 68.7%), and free cash flow compressed meaningfully. Regulatory headwinds (UK CMA probe, EU/US antitrust scrutiny) and the low 4.4% Copilot conversion rate (20M of 450M M365 subscribers) represent execution risks. On the positive side, Bill Ackman's new position, the upcoming Build conference catalyst, and the stock being the worst-performing Mag 7 name in 2026 (-12% YTD) create a modest rerating opportunity. The score reflects a high-quality franchise at a fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation with a credible near-term catalyst, but tempered by capex intensity and margin headwinds.
